The second-half record speaks for itself-four wins out of five, the fifth being a closing minute 7-6 loss to
Bay. At the close of the year, Ram officials tore up his contract which had another year to go and in its stead gave
the Dutchman a new three year agreement.
Clark broke into professional football with the Portsmouth (O.) Spartans in 193l after ending a brilliant col-
legiato career at Colorado College. 1932 saw him back there coaching, but the lure of the game proved too strong
and so Dutch was back again as field general of the Spartans in 1933. He moved over to Detroit when they picked
This marks Clark's ninth year with pro football, and his second as a non-player. His football record shows four
years of high school competition, the same number at Colorado College and eight years of professional football.
Nesring his thirty-fourth birthday, Clark leaves behind him a record of having been chosen All-National League
quarterback six times and the reputation of being called the greatest player the professional ranks have ever produced.
After football, Dutch likes golf. He is a member of Phi Gamma Delta fraternity, holds a B. A. degree. and makes
his home in Pueblo, 50 miles south of Colorado Springs, where he first made his bid for athletic recognition.
IGHT hand man to Coach Dutch Clark again is Art Lewis— ex-Ohio University, ex-New York Giant and starting his
R third year with the Rams.
Pappy, as he is affectionately known to the
boys, left an assistant coaching job at
Ohio Wesleyan to join the Rams in 1938 and subsequently took charge of the team early that season. Under the
leadership of Lewis the victory starved Rams suddenly did an about face and turned in three startling wins, the first
over the Detroit Lions (then being coached by.
Dutch) and the next two over the Chicago Bears. It was the first
time in the League's history that any team could boast two wins over the Bears in one season.
Lest year saw the formation of the Clark and Lewis combination for Cleveland. To Lewis went the task of whipping
into shape a formidable forward wall. Handicapped at the start of the season by green material and faced with a
dearth of reserves which was evident throughout the entire year Art brought into being a line which in the final half
of the season boasted of an amazing record. In those five games not one touchdown was made through the Ram line!
Although he played briefly last year, Lewis finally gave up his playing chores on advice from Dutch who placed
• high value on Art's ability as an
observer of play from the bench.
